headlines.title: Bank earnings live updates: AI dominates analyst calls from JPMorgan, Goldman and Wells Fargo
headlines.summary: Follow live bank earnings coverage for JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs and Citigroup, with third-quarter results, calls and stock moves.
headlines.article_text: Bank earnings October 2026: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Four of the largest U.S. banks reported third-quarter results on Tuesday: JPMorgan Chase , Wells Fargo , Goldman Sachs and Citigroup . Bank of America and Morgan Stanley will post earnings on Wednesday. The quarter was dominated by headlines around artificial intelligence, IPO uncertainty, high fuel prices and rising borrowing costs. The banks that reported Tuesday put up mixed results . JPMorgan, the biggest U.S. bank by assets and the largest in the world by market capitalization, posted a rare miss. Goldman Sachs, meanwhile, blew past estimates for revenue and earnings per share, led by strong equities trading. Analyst calls for JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo all touched on the opportunities and risks associated with AI, citing robust financing demand and operational advantages, but also the threat of rogue agents. Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon also addressed recent reports of a CEO transition plan. Here's what you need to know: JPM posts a rare earnings miss WFC is out with mixed results GS reports a massive revenue beat Citi's earnings report caps off the morning JPMorgan's CFO says deals are being 'delayed' Dimon says AI will 'benefit mankind enormously' Goldman CEO Solomon denies succession plans are in motion Moments Ago Citi sees consumer continuing to drive growth Citi's Fraser said on the call with analysts that macro environment conditions softened during the third quarter and that the "global economy has held up remarkably well." "In the U.S., while much has been made of the AI boom, the consumer is still driving much of the growth," she said. "The labor market is stable, and companies remain active. Our near-term economic outlook remains positive." She added that the bank's clients have remained "engaged" and "healthy." – Laya Neelakandan 1 Min Ago Citi CEO: Cyberdefense is a priority Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser said on a call with analysts on Tuesday that the company is focused on reducing systemic risk while deploying AI firm-wide. "Our cyberdefense strategy is about being on the front foot, about moving fast and retaining trust," Fraser said. "We don't wait for risks to happen. We're constantly preparing and improving our defenses. We're in the business of managing risk everyday, and this is no different." – Laya Neelakandan 2 Min Ago Investment banking fees mostly hold up watch now VIDEO 3:52 03:52 Goldman Sachs CEO says IPO market was 'a little bit softer in September' Squawk on the Street Investment banking fees at all four firms reporting on Tuesday largely held up during the third quarter, with most firms either matching or surpassing prior guidance. Still, the reports revealed declines on a quarter-over-quarter basis. At JPMorgan, investment banking revenue was up 14% year over year but down 8% quarter over quarter. JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum said the pipeline remains "very, very strong." Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon echoed that sentiment on his company's analyst call, while declining to say whether capital markets activity has peaked. That bank reported fees that were 21% higher from the prior year, but 5% lower than the second quarter. "IPOs that came in September were really the result of conversations in May and June around valuation expectations. Things got a little bit softer in September," Solomon said. "The IPO market was wide open. It's just if you expected a valuation and you got something 10 %to 15% less, you might choose not to go forward, you might choose to wait." Solomon added all the tech innovation and the AI infrastructure activity is a "real good ballast" for capital markets activity on a go-forward basis, noting that doesn't mean there won't be bumps. Citi posted the largest quarter-over-quarter decline in the fees, at 13% down. Wells Fargo reported investment banking revenue that was down 5% from the prior quarter. — Leslie Picker 15 Min Ago Goldman Sachs CEO sees growing risks in financing the AI infrastructure buildout Goldman Sachs Chairman and CEO David Solomon speaks at the Economic Club of New York in New York City, on June 2, 2026. Angela Weiss | AFP | Getty Images Solomon warned that the AI infrastructure boom could face a painful reset if higher borrowing costs or overbuilding undermine the economics of some data center projects. "There is going to be a lot of financing to do, and we're going to be in the middle of that," Solomon said during the bank's third-quarter call. "It may be that over time as the financing needs grow, that there's pressure on rates and that will affect the returns and the viability of certain projects," he said. "Not every project is going to be received as well." For now, demand for computing power remains strong and supply has yet to catch up, Solomon said, meaning more infrastructure will be built and more financing from Goldman and others will be needed. It's impossible to predict when a reset might happen or how the technology would evolve and be deployed, he said, calling the dynamic "an unknown we have to live with." "There will be a point in time when this recalibration resets, for sure," Solomon said. "When that does happen, of course there'll be some bumps." — Hugh Son 16 Min Ago Citigroup is beginning its conference call with analysts Citigroup, the final bank of the morning, is beginning its conference call with executives and analysts to discuss its third-quarter earnings results. – Laya Neelakandan 47 Min Ago Goldman CEO David Solomon denies succession plans are in motion John Waldron, chief operating officer of Goldman Sachs Group Inc., and Goldman Sachs Chairman and CEO David Solomon. Jason Alden | Bloomberg | Angela Weiss | AFP | Getty Images Goldman Sachs CEO Solomon pushed back against reports of an impending transition to executive chairman, saying Tuesday that no succession process or timeline is underway at the investment bank. Last month, news outlets cited anonymous sources that said Solomon would be replaced as CEO by Goldman President John Waldron as early as next year. The process would involve a vote by the bank's board that could happen in a matter of months, according to The Wall Street Journal. "I just want to be clear, there is no succession transition or timeline underway at Goldman Sachs," Solomon said during the bank's earnings call. "The board and I are singularly focused on our strategy to grow the firm and continue to serve our clients," he said. The CEO also pointed to the firm's future growth prospects, saying his leadership team was focused on expanding the franchise and accelerating its earnings growth in the coming years. "I have to say, at the point right now where we see the benefits of the effort that the broad team has made, I'm really enjoying the job," Solomon said. — Hugh Son 52 Min Ago Wells Fargo says demand for semiconductors continues to 'surge' Wells Fargo's Scharf said on the call with analysts that the AI investment cycle has become "a complicated macroeconomic force in its own right." "Demand for semiconductors, networking equipment, power generation, data center infrastructure, cooling systems, storage, cybersecurity and advanced manufacturing equipment continue to surge," Scharf said. "The scale of investment here increasingly resembles prior infrastructure booms, creating both significant opportunities but also risks given the significant leverage used to finance the build-out and the upward pressure on prices in selected industries and supply chains," he added. — Laya Neelakandan 56 Min Ago Wells Fargo CEO: Customer base remains strong Scharf said on the call with analysts that the company's customer base is "still strong." "Our underwriting criteria recognize that at some point consumer credit conditions will weaken," Scharf said. "To be clear, we do not see signs of this yet, but we know that cycles are inevitable." — Laya Neelakandan 57

headlines.article_text: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points UnitedHealth Group posted third-quarter earnings that blew past estimates and raised its full-year profit outlook. The nation's largest private insurer continues to manage high medical costs and is seeing investments in value-based care and artificial intelligence take hold, CFO Wayne DeVeydt said in an interview. The company said it expects fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings of at least $20.50 per share, up from a previous outlook of $19.50 to $20 per share. In this article UNH Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT UnitedHealth Group signage on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange on April 21, 2025. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images UnitedHealth Group on Tuesday posted third-quarter earnings that blew past estimates and raised its full-year profit outlook, as the company continues to manage high medical costs and sees investments in value-based care and artificial intelligence take hold. The nation's largest private insurer said it expects fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings of at least $20.50 per share, up from a previous outlook of $19.50 to $20 per share. The healthcare giant's turnaround plan is gaining momentum after three consecutive strong quarters this year. UnitedHealth is working to stabilize margins by shrinking membership, exiting unprofitable contracts, and ramping up investments in artificial intelligence and value-based care, which tie doctor and facility compensation to patient health outcomes, quality of care and cost effectiveness rather than the volume of medical services provided. "You'll see in the quarter that we continue to execute not only on the financial aspects of our business, but really doing them with a simpler approach and an approach that's really focused on investing heavily in value-based care," CFO Wayne DeVeydt said in an interview. Here's what the company reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: $4.69 adjusted vs. $4.14 expected Revenue: $112.69 billion vs. $111.40 billion expected The company posted third-quarter net income of $4.11 billion, or $4.56 per share, compared with $2.35 billion, or $2.59 per share, in the same period a year ago. Excluding items like business divestitures, restructuring and the expected reduction of reserves for unprofitable contracts, UnitedHealth earned $4.69 per share. Revenue fell to $112.69 billion from $113.16 billion a year earlier. The company's insurer, UnitedHealthcare, and its Optum healthcare unit both topped analysts' operating earnings estimates for the quarter, according to StreetAccount. Managing high costs Notably, UnitedHealth's medical cost ratio — a measure of total medical expenses paid relative to premiums collected — came in at 88.4% for the third quarter. Analysts were expecting a ratio of 89.9%, according to StreetAccount. A lower ratio typically indicates the company collected more in premiums than it paid out in benefits, resulting in higher profitability. Still, DeVeydt told CNBC that medical costs in the quarter "continue to be elevated versus historical norms" — an issue that has plagued insurers, particularly those operating privately run Medicare Advantage plans, for more than two years. "I think it's something we should keep an eye on. I think you'll see that our medical care ratio has improved quite a bit, but I don't want that to be misleading in terms of [medical cost trends]," DeVeydt said. He said the independent dispute resolution, or IDR, process under the No Surprises Act is adding at least 100 basis points, or 1 percentage point, to total medical costs. That federal law, which took effect in 2022, aims to protect consumers from unexpected medical bills. The IDR process allows providers and insurers to resolve disputes over out-of-network payments. DeVeydt said those changes are driving up the company's claims costs, which can ultimately be passed on to consumers through higher premiums. DeVeydt added that costs for inpatient services and pharmacy, particularly costly specialty pharmacy drugs for cancer and rare diseases, remain elevated. Still, he highlighted the company's value-based care efforts, which he said are helping control medical costs by steering patients toward the right providers and emphasizing preventive care, DeVeydt added. He said acute hospital admissions among UnitedHealth members fell 15% year over year through the third quarter, while home health admissions rose 10%, suggesting more patients are receiving care in lower-cost settings. "You're finding more members are actually getting into a lower-cost care environment, but more importantly, they're getting into the care environment they actually want to be in," he told CNBC. "So we think we're really balancing both the quality and the cost." UnitedHealth is also rolling out AI-powered ambient listening tools to reduce physicians' administrative burden and free up time for patient visits. Appointment scheduling done by patients rather than with the assistance of a provider increased 27% year over year, DeVeydt said. He expects those initiatives to have a compounding effect on medical cost management through the fourth quarter and into 2027 as the programs expand. headlines.summary: Technology stocks tumbled Tuesday as a sell-off in U.S. semiconductor shares spilled into Asian and European markets.
headlines.article_text: Micron, Seagate, Western Digital sink as chip sell-off deepens Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Chip stocks tumbled Tuesday, continuing to fall as the sell-off spilled into Asian and European markets. China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, reported progress on a new chip structure, intensifying chip competition. Intel and Broadcom CEOs have warned that access to capital could emerge as a major headwind to the artificial intelligence boom. In this article 9984.T-JP ASML STM IFX-DE SKHY Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Samuel Boivin | Nurphoto | Getty Images Chip stocks fell on Tuesday, extending a sell-off sparked by worries over artificial intelligence financing and intensifying competition. Memory chip giant Micron slipped about 5% while other memory-related names such as SanDisk , Seagate and Western Digital also sank. SanDisk fell 5% while Seagate and Western Digital both dropped 6%. The slide, which followed declines on Wall Street on Monday, comes as investors assessed intensifying competition from China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT . Over the weekend , CXMT announced significant progress in developing a new chip architecture, designed to increase memory density by packing more data into a smaller space. CXMT is China's leading rival to the likes of Micron and South Korean heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics . Analysts broadly see CXMT as trailing the U.S. and South Korean memory leaders, which means any advancement from the Chinese firm could add more competition to the market leaders. "Investors are jittery and looking for excuses to take profit on AI-related stocks that have outperformed this year, especially memory stocks," said UBP's senior equity advisor Vey-Sern Ling. "In reality, while the Chinese memory makers can potentially become a threat to global demand-supply balance over time, in the short run they continue to face technology hurdles, especially for more advanced memory like HBM," Ling told CNBC via email. CXMT shares closed 2.8% lower in Shanghai. Micron, Seagate, SanDisk, Western Digital stock chart. 'Vulnerable' AI sentiment? Phillip Wool, chief market strategist at Rayliant Global Advisors, said CXMT's breakthrough marked a significant milestone for Chinese chipmakers , demonstrating their ability to overcome technology restrictions and potentially challenge established players sooner than expected. But he cautioned that the market reaction appeared disproportionate to the immediate competitive threat, given that CXMT has yet to demonstrate large-scale production and continues to lag Samsung and SK Hynix in market share. "More importantly, we're not even talking about HBM here, and the Korean chipmakers are still unquestionably dominating that space, with very little threat at all from the likes of CXMT or anyone else for the foreseeable future," Wool said. He said the sharp sell-off reflected broader anxiety over the AI trade rather than a fundamental shift in the competitive landscape. "I read that more as a sign of how vulnerable AI sentiment is at this moment," Wool said, warning that volatility could persist as investors reassess chip demand and how long semiconductor manufacturers can sustain their pricing power. The chief executives of Intel and Broadcom have warned that access to capital could emerge as a major headwind to the AI boom, even as demand for computing infrastructure continues to outstrip supply. Investors are also looking ahead to a busy week of corporate earnings and U.S. inflation data, which could provide fresh clues on the outlook for interest rates that often have an inverse correlation with growth stocks. watch now VIDEO 4:30 04:30 Tech shakedown spreads as U.S. heavyweights face fresh selling Squawk Box Europe Global tech stocks slump Adding fuel to the sell-off was a post by Tesla and SpaceX boss Elon Musk, who said China has the ability to scale production once it figures out how to manufacture something. "When China figures out how to manufacture a product, their ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined," Musk said on Monday. European chip stocks also sank in early morning trade, with semiconductor equipment maker ASML down 3.3%, and STMicroelectronics and German chip maker Infineon both down 5%. Dutch firms BE Semiconductor and ASM International were both around 4% lower at the open. Shares of South Korean chip giant SK Hynix, a leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory chips used in artificial intelligence applications, plunged more than 10%, while rival Samsung Electronics shed 7.4% — both hitting their lowest levels since August. SK Hynix's U.S.-listed stock was down around 5% in premarket trading. In Japan, shares of tech-focused investment giant SoftBank Group sank 8.5%. The group, which has significant exposure to the global AI industry through its huge investment in OpenAI, led a broader retreat in Japanese semiconductor and electronics shares. Tokyo Electron , a major supplier of chipmaking equipment, dropped 7.2%, while Advantest , which makes semiconductor testing equipment, declined 2.9%. Other Japanese technology stocks also came under pressure. Lasertec fell over 5%, Disco lost 4.7% and Renesas Electronics shed 5.9%. The declines followed a weak session for technology stocks on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.44% on Monday. headlines.article_text: Apple releases HomeView smart home hub to showcase Siri AI Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Apple announced the new HomeView that starts at $299. The iPhone maker also announced the new Apple TV 4K and HomePod Mini. HomeView will act as a voice-controlled smart home hub for Apple devices and was built to showcase new Siri AI abilities. In this article AAPL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT John Ternus, chief executive officer of Apple Inc., during a product unveiling event at Apple Park in Cupertino, California, US, on Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Apple on Tuesday announced a new home hub called HomeView . Apple said the device with a 7-inch screen was designed to be mounted on a wall or placed on a table. It's designed for multiple people in a household, and will recognize the user by their face to display pertinent information. It starts at $299 and ships on Nov. 13. Tuesday's launch event is the second under new CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook in September. Last month, Apple announced new models of its most important product, the iPhone, including a foldable model called the Duo that retails for nearly $2,000. Apple also announced new Apple TV and HomePod hardware on Tuesday. The new Apple TV 4K costs $299 and has a redesigned remote that can play a sound if it is lost. Apple's HomePod Mini speaker comes in new colors and costs $149, a slight increase over its previous $129 price. The products announced Tuesday are less critical for Apple than the iPhone, and investors remain focused on iPhone sales, but the accessories were positioned on Tuesday as a showcase for the company's new Siri abilities released last month. Apple said that HomeView features Siri AI, which can answer a broad range of questions. Users will be able to converse with Siri, and their conversations will continue on their iPhone or iPad. It has a built-in speaker for playing music. Apple's HomeView can be placed on a table or mounted on a wall. Apple "It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home," Apple's chief marketer Greg Joswiak said in a statement. Apple said that HomeView will show information from the Messages, Photos, Calendar, and Reminders apps based on who is using the device, powered by Apple Intelligence. It can also be used to make FaceTime calls and as a digital photo frame. It's equipped with an Apple A18 chip. It supports up to six users. Apple TV, HomePods, and HomeView are included in Apple's Wearables, Home, and Accessories category, which reported $7.88 billion in sales in the most recent quarter ended June, which was about 7% of the company's total revenue. The category also includes wireless headphones like AirPods and the Apple Watch. But while Apple has dabbled in home products and platforms in the past, Tuesday's announcement shows Apple is making its home products a higher priority under Ternus. Apple said on Tuesday that its new products, including HomeView, can be used as a smart home hub, coordinating notifications and actions in the home and working with a range of products, including new locks, doorbells, and cameras from LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. Apple's integration with the smart home is not just about sales but also helps further lock customers into its own ecosystem. People who use multiple Apple products and connections are less likely to switch to an Android phone. HomeView can also become a smart home dashboard, Apple said. It can be used to view camera feeds, adjust the thermostat, or lock connected doors around the house. Apple said that setting up a new smart home device takes one tap from the user's iPhone. Tuesday's launch shows Apple's confidence as it launches new product categories. But the broader consumer electronics industry has been dealing with price increases and demand deterioration related to component shortages in memory and storage. It also comes as new boss Ternus has reportedly pushed the company to release products faster. Apple's new Apple TV 4K got a price hike from $199 to $299, and comes after a similar price increase earlier this year, after Cook said that memory costs for Apple were unsustainable.
